# MikroTik RouterOS (CRS-series switches and RouterOS-based devices) — Overview

## CLI dialect / platform scope

RouterOS's console is **structurally not the Cisco/Juniper mode-based CLI at all** — this is the single biggest cross-vendor contrast SignalScope needs to model correctly for this vendor.

- **No EXEC/config-mode split.** There is no `enable`, no `configure terminal`, no `interface X` sub-mode you "enter" and "exit." Instead the CLI is a **menu-path hierarchy**: every command is a path (`/interface`, `/interface bridge`, `/ip address`, `/snmp community`) followed by a sub-command (`print`, `add`, `set`, `remove`, `enable`, `disable`, `monitor`) and `key=value` arguments. E.g. `/interface bridge port set [find interface=ether3] pvid=20` is one self-contained command, not a multi-line "enter interface context, issue command, exit context" sequence the way Cisco/Huawei/Aruba require.
- You can either `cd` into a menu level interactively (prompt becomes `[admin@MikroTik] /interface bridge>`) and issue bare sub-commands there, or issue the fully-qualified path in one line from any level — both produce identical device state and identical audit-log text, which matters for SignalScope's "GUI action = literal CLI text" guarantee: there is no ambiguity about "what mode was I in" the way there is for Cisco's `interface`/`config-if` distinction.
- **Changes apply immediately as each command is entered** — there is no separate "config mode" buffer to commit or discard. Typing `/interface disable ether1` takes the port down the instant Enter is pressed, exactly like Cisco/Arista/Huawei's immediate-apply model (see [connectivity-methods.md](../../00-architecture/connectivity-methods.md)), but *without even the notion of a config-mode context* that those vendors have — RouterOS never distinguishes "I am editing configuration" from "I am running the router." One partial exception: **Safe Mode** (toggle with Ctrl+X in an interactive session, or `F4`) buffers changes made during that session and rolls them all back if the session disconnects before Safe Mode is turned off — a safety net for remote work, not a Juniper-style candidate-config requiring an explicit commit. Safe Mode is opt-in per session and off by default. [Console docs](https://help.mikrotik.com/docs/spaces/ROS/pages/8978498/Console), [CLI docs](https://help.mikrotik.com/docs/spaces/ROS/pages/328134/Command+Line+Interface).
- Scope: this covers RouterOS as used on MikroTik's CRS-series switches (CRS1xx/2xx/3xx/5xx) and general RouterOS-based devices (routers used as L2/L3 switches). RouterOS v7 is assumed as the primary target; v6 differences are called out where the bridge-VLAN model changed.

## SNMP version support and practical write scope

- **v1, v2c, and v3 are all supported** and can coexist (multiple `/snmp community` entries, some v1/v2c-style, SNMPv3 handled through the same community-table mechanism with added USM security parameters rather than a separate user table). [SNMP — RouterOS docs](https://help.mikrotik.com/docs/spaces/ROS/pages/8978519/SNMP), [SNMP — RouterOS Manual](https://manual.mikrotik.com/docs/diagnostics-monitoring-and-troubleshooting/snmp/), [Manual:SNMP (wiki, now redirects into help.mikrotik.com)](https://wiki.mikrotik.com/wiki/Manual:SNMP).
- **SNMP is historically, and still today, weighted toward monitoring/read use.** RouterOS documentation states plainly that "SNMP write access is only available for selected OIDs" — there is no general SNMP-driven configuration surface the way there might be an expectation of from an NMS. Confirmed real writable objects are narrow and mostly operational rather than structural:
  - `MIKROTIK-MIB::mtxrSystemReboot` (`1.3.6.1.4.1.14988.1.1.7.1.0`) — read-write, set non-zero to reboot the device.
  - `MIKROTIK-MIB::mtxrUSBPowerReset` (`1.3.6.1.4.1.14988.1.1.7.2.0`) — read-write, cut USB power for N seconds.
  - System identity (`SNMPv2-MIB::sysName`/`sysContact`/`sysLocation`) — standard MIB-II objects, writable per usual SNMPv2-MIB semantics.
  - Running a pre-configured script via SNMP SET, subject to the community/user's policy restrictions.
  - **No confirmed SNMP SET path exists for interface admin state, bridge/VLAN membership, spanning-tree parameters, or bonding** in MikroTik's own documentation or MIKROTIK-MIB (see `mib-reference.md`). Do not assume `IF-MIB::ifAdminStatus` SET works reliably on RouterOS the way it does on Cisco — it isn't documented by MikroTik as a supported write path; treat as **CLI-only** for this vendor pending device-level confirmation, per the architecture doc's "never assume an SNMP SET path" rule.
- Practical implication for SignalScope: for MikroTik devices, essentially every GUI-triggered configuration action should route through the CLI (SSH/API) session, not an SNMP SET fallback. SNMP's role for this vendor is telemetry/read-back and the small operational-write set above, not general config management.

## Config-apply model: no running/startup-config split

- RouterOS has **no `running-config` vs `startup-config` distinction at all.** There is a single, continuously-persisted configuration database on the device — every `add`/`set`/`remove`/`enable`/`disable` command writes directly to on-device storage as it executes. There is no equivalent of Cisco's `write memory` / `copy running-config startup-config`, and critically, **no "Save" step is needed or meaningful** for a RouterOS device the way it is for Cisco/Arista/Huawei/Aruba (persist-after-immediate-apply) or Juniper (explicit commit). A reboot without any separate save step will not lose configuration changes.
- What RouterOS *does* have, and what SignalScope should surface as "backup" rather than "save":
  - **`/system backup save [name=<file>]`** — writes a full binary snapshot of the configuration (and optionally system state) to a `.backup` file on device storage, restorable with `/system backup load`. This is a point-in-time binary snapshot, not something a human edits.
  - **`/export [file=<file>] [compact] [terse]`** — dumps the current configuration as a **replayable script** of the same CLI commands (`.rsc` text file) that recreate the current state, usable for version control/diffing (relevant to SignalScope's config-drift-detection tier — see [connectivity-methods.md](../../00-architecture/connectivity-methods.md)) or for re-applying config to another device. `/export` is the closer analogue to "show running-config" for diffing purposes, since it's human-readable text.
  - Neither of these is a prerequisite for a configuration change to take effect or survive reboot — they exist purely for backup/portability/audit, which is a genuinely different concept from every other vendor's "Save" button. This should be called out explicitly in SignalScope's GUI (see `gui-cli-snmp-mapping.md`).

## Distinctive introspection feature: `print oid`

RouterOS has a capability with no real equivalent among the other vendors covered so far: **`print oid`**, appended to almost any `print` command at almost any menu level, which returns the exact numeric OID(s) backing the values currently displayed at that menu level — live, from the device itself, without consulting any MIB file or browser.

- Example: `/interface print oid` → `name=.1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.2.1 mtu=.1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.4.1 ...` — confirms these map onto standard `IF-MIB::ifDescr`/`ifMtu` for interface index 1. ([Find MikroTik OIDs — Greg Sowell](https://gregsowell.com/?p=1419))
- Example: `/system health print oid` → `active-fan: .1.3.6.1.4.1.14988.1.1.3.9.0`, `voltage: .1.3.6.1.4.1.14988.1.1.3.8.0` — these line up exactly with `MIKROTIK-MIB::mtxrHlActiveFan` (`mtxrHealth.9`) and `MIKROTIK-MIB::mtxrHlVoltage` (`mtxrHealth.8`) in the vendored MIB (see `mib-reference.md`), confirming the technique is reliable for validating enterprise-MIB OIDs against a real device rather than trusting a possibly-stale downloaded MIB file.
- Other menus commonly walked this way per community documentation: `/system resource print oid`, `/system resource cpu print oid`, `/interface wireless print oid`. ([Community discussion](https://forum.mikrotik.com/t/snmp-oids/73480))
- **Why this matters for SignalScope's design**: this is a live device literally telling you its own OID mapping for whatever setting is on screen. For a vendor whose enterprise MIB (see below) has incomplete public documentation and whose numbering has grown organically over ~20 years of RouterOS releases, `print oid` is a far more reliable ground-truth source than any third-party MIB browser or vendored `.mib` file — SignalScope's MikroTik SNMP support (and any future auto-discovery of "does this OID exist/what does it mean on this exact firmware") should treat a live `print oid` query as the authoritative reconciliation mechanism, not just a nice-to-have CLI trick.

- [SNMP — RouterOS Manual](https://manual.mikrotik.com/docs/diagnostics-monitoring-and-troubleshooting/snmp/) — corroborating SNMP reference.
- [Manual:SNMP (wiki.mikrotik.com)](https://wiki.mikrotik.com/wiki/Manual:SNMP) — now 307-redirects into help.mikrotik.com's docs space; historical URL kept for citation continuity.
- [Command Line Interface — RouterOS](https://help.mikrotik.com/docs/spaces/ROS/pages/328134/Command+Line+Interface) and [Console — RouterOS](https://help.mikrotik.com/docs/spaces/ROS/pages/8978498/Console) — menu-path hierarchy, Safe Mode, no-config-mode behavior.
- [Bridging and Switching — RouterOS](https://help.mikrotik.com/docs/spaces/ROS/pages/328068/Bridging+and+Switching) — bridge/VLAN-filtering model, spanning-tree protocol-mode.

- [Basic VLAN switching — RouterOS](https://help.mikrotik.com/docs/spaces/ROS/pages/103841826/Basic+VLAN+switching) and [CRS1xx/2xx series switches examples](https://help.mikrotik.com/docs/spaces/ROS/pages/103841836/CRS1xx+2xx+series+switches+examples) — older switch-chip (`/interface ethernet switch`) VLAN model, for contrast.
- [Bonding — RouterOS](https://help.mikrotik.com/docs/spaces/ROS/pages/8323193/Bonding) — LACP/bonding syntax.
- [Switch Port Isolation (mikrotikdocs.fyi, community-maintained mirror)](https://mikrotikdocs.fyi/switch/switch-port-isolation/) and forum thread [CRS3xx Bridge horizon vs Switch port isolation](https://forum.mikrotik.com/t/crs3xx-bridge-horizon-vs-switch-port-isolation/179862) — port-isolation options (bridge `horizon` vs. hardware switch-chip isolation).
- [Find Mikrotik OIDs — Greg Sowell](https://gregsowell.com/?p=1419) and [MikroTik forum: SNMP oids](https://forum.mikrotik.com/t/snmp-oids/73480) — `print oid` worked examples.

## MIB licensing/redistribution note

- MikroTik publishes its own MIB file for download (currently versioned alongside RouterOS releases, e.g. `https://download.mikrotik.com/routeros/<version>/mikrotik.mib`, linked from [mikrotik.com/download/tools](https://mikrotik.com/download/tools)). That download page links only to MikroTik's general **"Export Eligibility Requirements and END USER LICENSE"** page (`mikrotik.com/software/legal`) — RouterOS's software EULA — with **no explicit, separate redistribution license for the MIB file itself**. Treat MikroTik's own MIB file as "downloadable for local use, redistribution terms unclear" — not vendored here for that reason.
- [LibreNMS](https://github.com/librenms/librenms) mirrors a `MIKROTIK-MIB` file at `github.com/librenms/librenms/blob/master/mibs/mikrotik/MIKROTIK-MIB` as part of its own device-support code. LibreNMS the project is licensed under **GPLv3** (confirmed via the repo's `LICENSE.txt`), which is a clear, explicit open-source license permitting redistribution with attribution and retention of the license text. This is a materially clearer redistribution basis than MikroTik's own download, so **this file is vendored here** (`mikrotik/mibs/MIKROTIK-MIB.txt`) with an attribution header pointing back to the LibreNMS source and its GPLv3 license — see `mibs/` below and the top-of-file note in the vendored copy.
- Caveat: the LibreNMS-mirrored copy is a snapshot (this session pulled the `master`-branch version, internally dated `202505190000Z`/2025-05-19) and may lag or lead the exact OID set on any given RouterOS version — cross-check against a live device's `print oid` output (see above) before trusting an OID number for anything write-path-critical.
